content.text: {"description":"What RoamSwitch watches per ATT&CK technique, assessed by reading its own code. A technique without a colour was not assessed (which is not the same as not covered). It states what is watched, not how well.","domain":"enterprise-attack","filters":{"platforms":["Linux","Windows","PRE","IaaS"]},"gradient":{"colors":["#e34a33","#fecc5c","#31a354"],"maxValue":2,"minValue":0},"hideDisabled":false,"layout":{"aggregateFunction":"average","countUnscored":false,"expandedSubtechniques":"none","layout":"side","showAggregateScores":false,"showID":true,"showName":true},"legendItems":[{"color":"#31a354","label":"Detects"},{"color":"#fecc5c","label":"Partial"},{"color":"#e34a33","label":"None"}],"links":[],"metadata":[],"name":"RoamSwitch Linux Client Edition: detection coverage","selectSubtechniquesWithParent":false,"selectTechniquesAcrossTactics":true,"selectVisibleTechniques":false,"showTacticRowBackground":false,"sorting":0,"tacticRowBackground":"#dddddd","techniques":[{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"The watchdog runs inside the daemon, so stopping or killing the daemon itself is not reported by it, and only guards that send a heartbeat are watched; a replaced RoamSwitch program file is caught by file integrity monitoring, a stopped service is not. Nothing checks that logging or telemetry paths stay open (blocking indicators, formerly T1562.006).","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"guardWatchdog, criticalPathFim"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1685"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"The guard re-creates its own nftables rules about every 20 seconds after an external flush, but it does not report the removal, and firewall rules that RoamSwitch did not create are not watched.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"portAnomalyGuard"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1686"},{"color":"#e34a33","comment":"The Linux audit system is not read or protected: stopping auditd, auditctl -e 0 and deleting audit rules are not watched.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"None"},{"name":"guards now","value":"not_applicable"}],"score":0,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1685.004"},{"color":"#e34a33","comment":"The Client Edition has no log tampering watch; the log audit reads logs for signs of attack but does not notice a log being emptied.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"None"},{"name":"guards now","value":"not_applicable"}],"score":0,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1685.006"},{"color":"#e34a33","comment":"Shell history files are not watched. The exec recorder keeps its own hash-chained record of executed commands, so clearing the history does not erase what ran, but the clearing itself is not reported.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"None"},{"name":"guards now","value":"not_applicable"}],"score":0,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1070.003"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only running a program from a deleted file (EXR-002) and the deletion of files on the critical-path list are reported; deleting any other file is not. The security report's fileless check also lists a running program whose file is gone from /tmp, /home, /root, /srv, /var/www or /opt when nothing replaced it, but only at the moment a report is made.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder, criticalPathFim"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1070.004"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Changes to /etc/ld.so.preload and the linker configuration are caught (and the next program run after such a change, EXR-007). LD_PRELOAD or LD_AUDIT naming a library outside the system directories, or LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at a writable directory, is caught when a service, or a service account, starts a program (EXR-013). Replaced shared libraries, and the environment of a process that was already running, are not seen.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"criticalPathFim, execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1574.006"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"A command that an AI coding agent (claude, codex, gemini, opencode, aider, goose, cursor-agent, openclaw, qwen, crush) starts as a child process and that sends a credential file or a secret value out (curl with -T or -d, scp or rsync to a remote host, rclone, aws s3 cp, nc and the like) is reported (EXR-014), and so is a send within five minutes of a command of the same agent reading credential files (EXR-015). Only commands the agent starts as child processes are seen: the agent's own file reads, what it sends to its model provider, git push and connections that a script runtime opens itself are not, and neither is an agent whose process name is node. Notify-only.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1048"},{"color":"#e34a33","comment":"Process names, paths and file names that imitate system ones are not checked.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"None"},{"name":"guards now","value":"not_applicable"}],"score":0,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1036"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Yama restricts ptrace between unrelated processes only on kernels that have it active; writes through /proc/<pid>/mem, LD_PRELOAD and other injection methods are neither prevented nor detected. The only injection report is a debugger attached by a service account (T1055.008).","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"off"},{"name":"covered by","value":"yamaMemoryProtect"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1055"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only gdb, strace or ltrace started with a process id by a service account, or by a non-root user under a service process, is reported (EXR-012); other tools, root, and ordinary login sessions are not, and the attach itself is not watched, only the command line at start.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1055.008"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Signatures see only known byte patterns, so packed or encrypted payloads pass; at run time only decode-and-run one-liners (EXR-004, including a shell named through $SHELL and Python os.system) and autostart entries that decode into an interpreter are recognized.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"webMailDownloadGuard, clamavScan, execRecorder, persistenceWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1027"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only an exec from an anonymous memory file (memfd) is caught (EXR-002); code loaded into memory by a program that is already running, without a new exec, is not seen.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1620"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Package-managed unit directories (/usr/lib/systemd) are deliberately not watched, and a new unit that looks ordinary is only logged, not notified.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch, criticalPathFim"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1543.002"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"A new cron entry that looks ordinary is only logged, not notified.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch, criticalPathFim, execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1053.003"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only lines that look like how malware persists are notified (a reverse shell, decode-and-run, download-and-run, a program run from a temporary folder). A line that was already in the file when the watch started is not reported, and the start-up files of other shells such as csh and tcsh are not watched.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1546.004"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"The .pth files, sitecustomize.py and usercustomize.py in the interpreters' site folders and in virtual environments under a home folder (found to a depth of four folders, again every minute), and the module a .pth file imports from its own folder. Only code that reads three or more kinds of credential store, decodes data and runs it, runs what it downloaded, or has the shape of a reverse shell is notified; a module that hides its strings is not seen. Environments inside containers and below the fourth folder are not watched.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1546.018"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only /etc/udev/rules.d is watched, not the rules that packages install, and only RUN and PROGRAM commands that look like how malware persists are notified.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1546.017"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only the settings in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d are read (such as the Invoke hooks that run a command around apt and dpkg); the hooks of dnf, zypper and pacman are not watched, and only commands that look like how malware persists are notified.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1546.016"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"The hooks git itself would run (a hook name such as pre-commit or post-checkout with an execute bit; the *.sample files are left out) in the .git/hooks of the working copies under each home folder (found to a depth of six folders, or up to twelve with git_hook_scan_depth in config.json; not entering a repository; searched again at least every minute and never more than about 1% of the time), including the submodules (.git/modules) and the working copies in ~/.config, ~/.local/share, ~/.dotfiles, ~/.oh-my-zsh and a few other hidden folders where tools keep them, in the folder core.hooksPath names in a repository's own .git/config or in the global or system git configuration (~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/git/config, /etc/gitconfig and the files they include), and in ~/.git-templates/hooks and ~/.config/git/hooks. Only lines that look like how malware persists are notified, and a line that was already in the hook when the watch started is not reported. A working copy deeper than the scan depth or in any other hidden folder, and a relative core.hooksPath in a global configuration, are not watched; a scan that hits the limit of 1,000 working copies or 30,000 folders per home is shown as a gap in the coverage map.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1546"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only /etc/rc.local, the scripts in /etc/init.d and in /etc/update-motd.d, /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d and ~/.ssh/rc are read, and only commands that look like how malware persists are notified.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"persistenceWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1037.004"},{"color":"#e34a33","comment":"The Client Edition keeps no inventory of SUID/SGID files.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"None"},{"name":"guards now","value":"not_applicable"}],"score":0,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1548.001"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only authorized_keys and authorized_keys2 in the .ssh folder of login accounts and /root/.ssh are watched; keys in a location set by sshd's AuthorizedKeysFile, or served by AuthorizedKeysCommand, are not.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"criticalPathFim"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1098.004"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only reads are seen, and a program that runs under an allowlisted name (for example python3 for ~/.aws, or a script run by node for an AI agent's own sign-in file) is not reported. Watched: ssh keys, ~/.aws, gcloud, browser stores, the sign-in files of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and opencode, GitHub Copilot's hosts.json and apps.json, the GitHub CLI's hosts.yml, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.netrc and ~/.pgpass. Not watched: ~/.kube/config, ~/.docker/config.json and ~/.azure, which every Kubernetes, container and Azure tool opens on each command, and any other credential file. The decoys only show a read of the decoys.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"credentialAccessWatch, honeytokens"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1552.001"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Decoy files trip only when touched. The entropy-burst heuristic judges the whole file, 4 KiB windows and, in a pattern, 256-byte windows of the first 256 KiB, so it can miss slow encryption, blocks as small as 16 bytes, and changes past the first 256 KiB. A file written to a temporary name and renamed over the original is judged too, but a ciphertext put in place by a separate cp or mv command is not counted.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"ransomwareCanaryGuard, entropyFreeze"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1486"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only btrfs subvolume delete and lvremove run by something other than a known snapshot manager are recognized (EXR-008); other ways of removing recovery points, such as deleting backup files, are not.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1490"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Heuristic and notify-only: bursts of long, high-entropy labels or TXT/NULL queries (10 within 60 seconds); slow or low-entropy tunnels and DNS over HTTPS are not seen.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"linkGuard"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1071.004"},{"color":"#e34a33","comment":"The Client Edition does not read DNS replies, so it does not see names being enumerated.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"None"},{"name":"guards now","value":"not_applicable"}],"score":0,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1590.002"},{"color":"#e34a33","comment":"The Client Edition does not watch connections to the cloud metadata address.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"None"},{"name":"guards now","value":"not_applicable"}],"score":0,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1552.005"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Alert only: nothing is isolated or killed. A finding needs two scans in a row (every 2 seconds), and private-range peers are watched only when opted in. A shell whose standard input and output are not one outbound TCP or UDP connection is matched only when it is wired both ways to an interpreter, openssl, telnet, ssh or a relay tool that holds the connection and does not listen (reported as a lower-severity warning); a relay through a third program such as cat is not matched. The exec recorder (EXR-011) also reports known command-line shapes at start, which does not cover a shell started any other way.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"reverseShellWatch, execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1059.004"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only a shell or interpreter one-liner started by a service account from a service process is caught (EXR-001); a web shell that runs code inside the web server process without starting a program is not seen.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1505.003"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only a process seen with uid 0 and no setuid binary or capability in its ancestry is flagged (EXR-005); an exploit that never starts a process after gaining root is not seen.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1068"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only curl|sh style pipes and a downloaded file executed within the time window (default 120 seconds) are linked (EXR-003), for curl, wget and tnftp/ftp with -o, including combined flags such as curl -fsSLo and wget -qO; a download that is run later, or fetched by another client, is not.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"execRecorder"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1105"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Follows sshd's log only, and only while sshd is running: guessing against other services is not counted. A lost journal cursor, a truncated log or a log that cannot be read leaves a gap that liveState and the collectors record show; with no readable log nothing is banned.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"on"},{"name":"covered by","value":"sshGuard"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1110.001"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Compares the kernel's ARP table over time and flags one MAC answering for several IPs; a forged entry that is replaced and restored between two reads is not seen, and an unreadable table skips that cycle (counted) and keeps the baseline.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"arpSpoofAutoContainment"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1557.002"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Once a minute the DHCP servers, gateways and DNS servers in the host's own lease files (NetworkManager, systemd-networkd, ISC dhclient) are compared with the earlier leases of the same network, and a new one is reported once. The same is done for the IPv6 side of each network: the default routers accepted from router advertisements, the DNS servers accepted through DHCPv6 or RDNSS, and the DHCPv6 server; and for a DHCP option 252 (WPAD) address the network had not handed out before (kept by NetworkManager always, by ISC dhclient and systemd-networkd only when asked for it). A forged offer that the DHCP client did not accept (nothing of it stays on the host; the Sensor watches the network for those), the first lease of a new network, and a value the network used before are not reported.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"networkSettingWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1557.003"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only a new proxy auto-configuration (a PAC script address or WPAD detection) in Firefox, KDE, NetworkManager connections or an auto_proxy environment setting is reported, once; GNOME's own proxy setting is not read. Forged LLMNR, NBNS and mDNS answers on the network are not seen: the security report only shows whether this host has an LLMNR or NBNS responder bound.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"networkSettingWatch"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1557.001"},{"color":"#fecc5c","comment":"Only npm projects in the registered folders are looked at: a lockfile that changed, install-time code (a script or compiled code) that was added since the state you accepted, and a dependency name close to a popular package. Nothing says whether a dependency is malicious, a project with no accepted state is not compared (you are told once), and the other ecosystems (PyPI, crates.io and the rest) have no such watch.","enabled":true,"links":[],"metadata":[{"name":"coverage","value":"Partial"},{"name":"guards now","value":"unknown"},{"name":"covered by","value":"npmSupplyWatch, lockfileFim"}],"score":1,"showSubtechniques":false,"techniqueID":"T1195.001"}],"versions":{"attack":"20","layer":"4.5","navigator":"4.9.5"}}
